scenes.headline: How Timestral turns a series into quantile forecasts
scenes.sub: Patches, a causal trunk, and separate forecast tokens
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Galloon! Timestral reads a stream of numbers and answers with a spread of possible futures. Here is how.

scenes.text: Cut the history into patches, read them with a causal transformer, and let separate forecast tokens ask for the future as 21 quantiles.
scenes.say: Cut the history into patches, read them causally, and let separate forecast tokens ask for the future.

items.say: Cut it into patches of thirty-two steps. Each patch is a token.
Scale each patch by what came before it, never after.
Squash it, so a huge spike arrives small.
And flag every missing value, so a gap stays a gap.

steps.say: The patches enter a twenty-four layer trunk. Each one reads only itself and earlier patches.
Then come forecast tokens, copies of one learned vector. They read the whole context. The context never reads them.
A head turns each forecast token into twenty-one quantiles per step, built so they cannot cross.
Every fourth layer also looks across the series' other variables.

scenes.title: How a quantile is trained
scenes.say: Each quantile is trained with the pinball loss.

parts.note: truth above the forecast costs tau per unit
parts.say: Truth above the forecast costs tau per unit missed.

parts.note: truth below costs one minus tau
parts.say: Truth below costs one minus tau. So the forecast settles where a fraction tau falls under it.

scenes.title: Seconds per forecast, two CPU threads
scenes.say: On two shared CPU threads, even the full context took six and a half seconds. It is only about a thousand tokens.

scenes.text: A 32,768-step context is only 1,024 patch tokens. That is why a 209M forecaster runs on a CPU.
scenes.say: So remember: thirty-two thousand steps is only about a thousand tokens. That is why it runs on a CPU.
